summary: SplitSync iteration 6 (security hardening) backend testing complete. All 25 new pytest cases pass (25/25) and the full serial suite passes 119/119 in ~193s via `pytest -n 0`. Verified: (1) POST /api/scan with base64 length > 5,500,000 returns 413 with generic 'Image too large' in <5s (LLM not invoked); (2) per-user hourly rate limit — using a dedicated seed user (TEST_scan_rl_iter6@example.com / bearer TEST_scan_rl_token_iter6) 20 tiny valid JPEG scans (48x32 with features/text/line) all succeed, 21st returns 429 with 'rate limit' in detail; primary test user (test_token_abc) still returns 200/502 on scan proving buckets are per-user; (3) LLM failure surface — 502 responses carry only generic 'AI extraction failed' text, no Traceback / server file path / stack details leaked; if the LLM tolerated garbage the response is still non-leaky; (4) POST /api/expenses amount=0 and amount=-1 both return 400 with 'amount must be > 0'; (5) currency='XYZ' returns 400 with 'currency' + supported list; (6) receipt_image_base64 > 5,500,000 returns 413; (7) valid USD amount=10 regression passes and is persisted (Create→GET verified); (8) POST /api/recurring: amount<=0 → 400, currency='XYZ' → 400, cadence='daily' → 400, valid monthly USD 15.0 accepted and persisted; (9) CORS preflight (OPTIONS with Origin+ACRM) returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin=* AND Access-Control-Allow-Credentials absent (verified None), Access-Control-Allow-Methods includes GET, POST, DELETE, OPTIONS; (10) Regression battery: /api/auth/me, /api/friends, /api/groups, /api/settlements, /api/expenses, /api/insights, /api/trends (months=6, series length 6), /api/fx (5 currencies), and /api/expenses/{id}/receipt round-trip all still succeed. Legacy iter1-5 (94 tests) remain fully green.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to 921 lines; splitting into routers (auth, expenses, friends, groups, recurring, settlements, fx, scan, insights, trends) is now overdue and would make security invariants (size cap + rate limit) easier to audit.

Rate-limit state (_SCAN_HITS) is in-process memory only. Under multi-worker deployment (gunicorn/uvicorn workers>1) the 20/hour cap is per-worker not per-user globally; consider Mongo TTL bucket or Redis if you ever scale horizontally.
SCAN_RATE_PER_HOUR and MAX_RECEIPT_B64_LEN are module constants; consider exposing via env vars so security thresholds can be tuned without redeploying code.
Currency validation duplicated in /expenses, /recurring, /auth/currency — extract a `_validate_currency(cur)` helper to keep the supported set enforced in one place.

Size check on /expenses receipt_image_base64 short-circuits after amount/currency validation but BEFORE any DB call — good. Consider adding the same `Field(max_length=…)` on the Pydantic model so FastAPI can 422 earlier and skew away from custom 413 mapping.
Emergent LLM chat currently uses `gemini-3-flash-preview`; if that preview is deprecated/removed the /scan endpoint will 502 constantly. Consider a fallback model or graceful degradation.
logger.exception in /scan writes full stack to backend logs (correct), but the HTTPException detail 'AI extraction failed' is fine — no leak. No change needed, just confirming intent.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 6 fully validated. Run: `cd /app/backend && pytest tests/ -n 0 -v` for deterministic serial (all 119 pass in ~3m13s). The rate-limit test alone takes ~110s because it fires 21 real LLM scans on tiny JPEGs; if EMERGENT_LLM_KEY quota is tight, this test consumes ~21 gemini-3-flash-preview requests per run. Rate-limit state is in-memory (_SCAN_HITS) — restarting the backend resets buckets, so iter6 can be safely retried after `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`. Size cap constant: MAX_RECEIPT_B64_LEN=5_500_000 (server.py L25). Hourly cap constant: SCAN_RATE_PER_HOUR=20 (server.py L26). Order-of-operations guaranteed by server.py L809-821: size-check (413) → rate-limit (429) → LLM call (200/502) — so an oversized request will NOT consume a slot. CORS: allow_credentials=False, methods=['GET','POST','DELETE','OPTIONS'], allow_origins=['*'], allow_headers=['*'] (server.py L913-920). Supported currencies: USD, INR, EUR, GBP, JPY. Supported cadences: monthly, weekly.
rca_of_issue: No product bugs found. Only a test-authoring miss during first run: initial LLM-failure-surface test assumed the response would always be JSON with a 'detail' key, but when the primary user was already at its rate limit the response was a plain 429/text body, so `r.json()` raised JSONDecodeError. Fixed by reading `r.text` first, checking for stack-trace leaks on ANY body, and only attempting JSON parse when status is 502 (with try/except fallback). This makes the test tolerant of three legitimate outcomes: (a) 502 generic 'AI extraction failed', (b) 200 LLM tolerated garbage, (c) 429 already rate-limited — all acceptable as long as no server internals leak.
